user_query: I was arrested for shoplifting. What happens now?
variations: I got caught stealing, what will happen?
Arrested by police, what are my rights?
Will I go to jail for stealing?
part_a_general_info: After arrest, police will investigate. Depending on the circumstances, several outcomes are possible: a stern warning, a composition fine (for compoundable offences), a conditional warning, or being charged in court. For minor offences (e.g., first-time shoplifting of low value), a composition fine or conditional warning is possible. If charged in court, you will need to decide whether to plead guilty or claim trial. You can submit a mitigation plea if pleading guilty. You may be eligible for legal aid through the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS) or the Public Defender's Office (PDO) if you cannot afford a lawyer.
triage_questions: Q1: What were you arrested for? What are the specific charges?
Q2: Is this your first offence?
Q3: Have you given a statement to the police?
Q4: Have you been formally charged in court?
Q5: Can you afford a lawyer?
branching_logic: If Q2 = first offence, minor charge → Composition or conditional warning may be possible.
If Q4 = not yet charged → Still under investigation. May receive offer of composition.
If Q5 = cannot afford → Refer to CLAS/PDO.
routing: Route A (Not yet charged, minor offence): Advise to cooperate with investigation. Inform about possibility of composition/warning. Refer to CLAS for legal advice.
Route B (Charged in court): Refer to CLAS or PDO for legal representation. Provide information on means test and merits test.
Route C (Serious offence): Urgent referral to CLAS/PDO. If drug offence, inform about mandatory minimum sentences.
guardrail: Must NOT advise on plea (guilty/not guilty) or assess the merits of any defence.
